newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU spirits producers welcome Japan drink ruling.
newsitem.headline: EU spirits producers welcome Japan drink ruling.

text.p: Europe's spirits producers on Friday welcomed the World Trade Organisation (WTO) Dispute Settlement Body panel ruling on a long-standing complaint that Japanese liquor taxes discriminate against European imports.

The European Confederation of Spirits Producers, which has fought against the system, said Japan should now set up a single liquor tax category with a specific rate of tax for all distilled spirits based on alcohol content.
"Such taxation is consistent with prevailing practice within the EU, Canada, the United States and other OECD countries," the confederation's director general Gillian Darley said in a statement.

"We thereforce urge the new Japanese government to grasp the nettle and implement this system in its budget for 1997. By doing ao Japan would be seen to be resolving this long-standing issue in a positive manner and as evidence of its free trade credentials"
A majority of the Geneva-based WTO's 125 member states were present for the closed-door meeting and no one challenged the quorum on the report, he added.
After the neutral WTO panel reached its decision on October 4, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said Japan would consider making tax changes later this year in the context of a broader review.

The WTO Dispute Settlement Body adopted the report on a complaint by the European Union, United States and Canada that tax differentials on liquor sold in Japan effectively favour the popular domestic shochu over imported whisky and other spirits.
